title: Bootstrapped CPC rule of thumb: max click bid = ARPU/25
summary: Jason gives a pre-data formula for bootstrapped SaaS founders deciding how much to pay per click. Assume 20-month customer life, CAC at one fifth of LTV (four months of revenue), and 1% visitor-to-paid conversion. That gives max CPC = ARPU/25, which also argues for charging more.

principles.text: With no data, bootstrapped founders should assume a 20-month customer life; a low LTV guess is safer than an inflated one.
principles.quote: a good **pre-data rule of thumb is 20 months**.

principles.text: Keep CAC at LTV/5, stricter than the funded-company LTV/3, because early cheap channels exist but saturate.
principles.quote: I urge profit-seekers to instead adopt an even more strict model of CAC = LTV / 5.

principles.text: CAC should be no more than four months of revenue, so payback is about four months (three if you collect month one upfront).
principles.quote: the cost to acquire a customer should be no more than four months of revenue.

principles.text: Profit-seeking bootstrappers can't afford CAC > LTV or 'land-grab' justifications; funded firms can pay to find out, you can't.
principles.quote: Profit-seeking bootstrapped companies cannot afford those delusions.

principles.text: Assume 1% visitor-to-paying conversion pre-data, so max CPC = ARPU/25 (e.g. $50/mo ARPU allows $2/click).
principles.quote: So for example if your average customer generates $50/mo, you can spend $2/click.

principles.text: Charge more than you think: higher ARPU lets you pay more per click, opens more channels and outbids low-LTV competitors.
principles.quote: **you should charge a lot more than you think**, in part because it enables you to pay quite a lot per click
